product: commentary — no product (a creative director describing static concepts, not a live ad)
hook: "Three static concepts from one angle (energy), none of them showing the product" — concept-pack framing.
body: Concept 1, "The calendar": a week view with "gym," "dinner with friends," "hike" all crossed out; headline "this is what 'I'm just tired' is actually costing you." Concept 2, "The text thread": "Sorry, can't make it..." (post truncated, third concept not in file).
idea: The cross-out visual doesn't have to list failed products — crossing out the LIFE the problem costs you (gym, friends, hike) makes the pain concrete and personal.
sequencing: The frame (three concepts, one angle, no product shown)
The missing third concept (not in file — truncated)
why_it_works: Crossing out calendar events weaponizes loss aversion — the viewer sees their own cancelled plans, which is a more visceral pain than a list of failed products.
what_to_steal: LC's "cost of tarnish" calendar: crossed-out "beach day," "pool party," "gym" with the headline "this is what cheap jewelry is costing you" — then the waterproof piece as the fix.

product: commentary — no product (a format-catalog methodology post)
hook: "The first version of this list was 40 screenshots from the ad library. Half of them were dead by the time I went back to check." — methodology drama.
body: Rebuilt a 37-format list with proof: one live ad per format, days running + brand's active ad count next to each; the 30-day survival column is the "this works" bar — anything under is still a test. Links to a Notion doc and a GetHookd board (132 ads).
cta: "One doc. You can sort it by days running. No comment or follow needed" (doc links).
idea: Format validation should be survival-based, not screenshot-based — an ad that survived 30 days of real spend is proven; everything else is a test.
sequencing: The failure of v1 (40 screenshots, half dead)
The proof columns (live ad, days running, brand ad count)
The rule (copy the structure, not the words)
formatting: Text post; hand-graded VALUE status, 18 bookmarks.
why_it_works: The 30-day survival bar is a simple, falsifiable quality filter — it turns "formats that work" from opinion into a sortable column.
what_to_steal: The survival-bar discipline for LC's format testing: a format earns "proven" status only after 30 days of live spend — everything else stays in test.

product: commentary — no product (a format-list post; cross-out is #6 of 37)
hook: "There are 37 ad formats printing right now." — authority list promise.
body: Lists 10 of the 37 formats (AI podcast, report card, iPhone Notes, text on skin, Reddit style, the cross-out, fake PDP, tier list, myth vs fact, zero stars); notes the longest-running was an AI podcast ad at 280 days; links the full doc with live ad + days active + brand ad count per format.
cta: Doc links ("No comment or follow needed").
idea: "The cross-out" is one of 37 verified money-making formats — its inclusion in a survival-filtered list is itself the proof of the format.
sequencing: The doc pitch (live ad + days + count per format)
formatting: Text post + photo; 110 likes, 208 bookmarks — the most-bookmarked format post in the slice.
why_it_works: The numbered-list format is inherently skimmable and saveable, and the days-active proof column gives each format a credibility anchor most "format" posts lack.
what_to_steal: Cross-out's verified-format status justifies LC prioritizing it (the folder README already rates it P1) — and the "copy the structure, not the words" rule for LC's version.

product: commentary — no product (a computer-vision research post over 4,617 static ads)
hook: "I analyzed 4,617 top-performing static ads with AI vision. Here is the unfiltered data on what actually converts in 2026" — dataset-scale authority.
body: Multimodal pipeline (SigLIP embeddings, HDBSCAN clustering, OCR, Gemini layout deconstruction) over 4,617 paid-social statics; macro findings (54.1% product-only/zero faces, 53% pain-point-first hooks, only 13% show price, 11.3% discount codes); 5 debunked myths; 8 layout archetypes; 7 proof devices; the native-disguise phenomenon (12.4%); 4 emerging hacks — including #4 "The Strikethrough Price Anchor" ($120 ➢ $49 crossed-out MSRP); plus a 2026 static blueprint and publish checklist.
cta: "Bookmark this post if you're building creative for Meta, TikTok, or LinkedIn this quarter."
idea: Strikethrough is a proven micro-tactic at dataset scale — when prices appear, winners show a crossed-out anchor MSRP, not just the final price; and 53% of winners lead with pain-point resolution, which is the cross-out static's native territory.
sequencing: Macro findings (faces, hooks, price, discounts, native UI)
Myth 1 (discount codes) → sell relief, not price
formatting: Very long text post + 4 photos; research-report structure with data tables.
why_it_works: Dataset scale (4,617 ads, named methods) makes every claim feel empirical rather than opinionated — it reads as the closest thing to ground truth the feed offers.
what_to_steal: Two cross-out-relevant findings: (a) always show the crossed-out anchor price ($120 ➢ $49) on LC sale statics; (b) 53% pain-first hooks validates LC's cross-out angle (cross out the failed fixes, lead with the frustration).
